question: Should Reef core permanently own and support the Kubernetes/PostgreSQL relay as an equal adapter alongside Cloudflare?
rationale: The branch is technically coherent, but it expands the authoritative architecture, persistent data model, release surface, and compatibility obligations; tests cannot decide whether maintainers want that permanent product boundary.

options.title: Sponsor the core adapter
options.body: Accept Kubernetes/PostgreSQL as a supported Reef platform, require the requested real-cluster proof, and review future changes against the shared compatibility contract.

options.title: Keep Cloudflare-only core
options.body: Decline the second core platform and ask that the portable relay live in a separately maintained deployment project or fork while preserving any generally useful shared-core refactor separately.

options.title: Narrow the proposal
options.body: Pause the full adapter and first land only the platform-neutral contract extraction if maintainers want that foundation without committing to PostgreSQL and Helm ownership yet.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the core adapter
recommendation.body: Accept Kubernetes/PostgreSQL as a supported Reef platform, require the requested real-cluster proof, and review future changes against the shared compatibility contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The current authoritative design records Peter as the product-design approver, so he is the strongest available routing candidate for this scope decision.
